loss_shapes.caption: Loss is zero exactly on the diagonal ŷ = y, where the prediction is right. It depends only on the residual ŷ − y, so the trough looks the same all along the diagonal: a parabola. Big misses cost quadratically more, which is why MSE chases outliers.
loss_shapes.slice: y = 0: along the prediction axis, ŷ is the residual.
loss_shapes.title: Mean squared error over truth and prediction

loss_shapes.caption: Loss is zero on the diagonal ŷ = y and grows in straight lines either side: a V-shaped trough. The sharp crease at the bottom has no gradient, and every miss costs in proportion to its size, so a few outliers can't dominate.
loss_shapes.slice: y = 0: along the prediction axis, ŷ is the residual.
loss_shapes.title: Mean absolute error over truth and prediction

loss_shapes.caption: A trough along ŷ = y whose bottom is rounded like MSE within δ of the diagonal and whose walls are straight like MAE beyond it. δ sets where the quadratic part ends: small errors are treated gently, outliers linearly.
loss_shapes.slice: y = 0: along the prediction axis, ŷ is the residual.
loss_shapes.title: Huber loss over truth and prediction

loss_shapes.caption: Loss is high where truth and prediction disagree: predicting q near 0 when p is 1, or near 1 when p is 0, costs without bound (heights are capped). The valley follows q = p, but its floor is the entropy H(p), not zero: even a perfect forecast of a 50/50 outcome pays ln 2. Remove the entropy to see the KL divergence, which is zero exactly when q = p.
loss_shapes.slice: p = 1: along the predicted-probability axis, with margin m = ln(q / (1 − q)).
loss_shapes.title: Binary cross-entropy over true and predicted probability

loss_shapes.caption: Hinge loss depends only on the gap z_correct − z_other, so the surface is a sheet folded along that direction. It is flat (zero) once the correct class wins by the margin, and rises linearly when it doesn't: it stops caring about examples it already gets right.
loss_shapes.slice: z_other = 0: along the correct-class axis, z_correct is the margin.
loss_shapes.title: Hinge loss over two class scores

loss_shapes.caption: Like hinge, a sheet folded along the gap between the scores, flat once the correct class wins by the margin. Below the margin it rises quadratically, so badly wrong examples are pushed much harder.
loss_shapes.slice: z_other = 0: along the correct-class axis, z_correct is the margin.
loss_shapes.title: Squared hinge loss over two class scores

loss_shapes.caption: A smooth version of hinge: it depends only on the gap z_correct − z_other, never quite reaches zero, and keeps nudging even confident correct answers. This is softmax cross-entropy for two classes, and the same loss as binary cross-entropy on probabilities.
loss_shapes.slice: z_other = 0: along the correct-class axis, z_correct is the margin.
loss_shapes.title: Logistic (softmax) loss over two class scores

loss_shapes.caption: A cliff: loss is 1 wherever the other class scores at least as high, and 0 wherever the correct class wins. It counts mistakes exactly, but it is flat everywhere else, so it has no gradient to learn from. Smooth losses exist because of this.
loss_shapes.slice: z_other = 0: along the correct-class axis, z_correct is the margin.
loss_shapes.title: 0-1 loss over two class scores

loss_shapes.caption: Every row is a Huber curve for one δ. Small δ makes Huber behave like a scaled absolute error; large δ makes it a squared error over the whole range. The bend where the parabola meets the straight walls slides outward as δ grows.
loss_shapes.slice: The row at the requested hyperparameter value.
loss_shapes.title: Huber loss over residual and δ

loss_shapes.caption: Every row is a hinge curve for one margin parameter. The crease where the loss becomes zero sits at m = μ, so a larger margin parameter demands that the correct class win by more before the loss stops.
loss_shapes.slice: The row at the requested hyperparameter value.
loss_shapes.title: Hinge loss over margin and the margin parameter

loss_shapes.caption: Every row is a squared-hinge curve for one margin parameter. The flat region starts at m = μ; below it the loss grows quadratically, so moving the margin moves where the bowl begins.
loss_shapes.slice: The row at the requested hyperparameter value.
loss_shapes.title: Squared hinge loss over margin and the margin parameter

loss_shapes.caption: With three classes, a prediction is a point on a triangle q₁ + q₂ + q₃ = 1; class 1 is the true one. Cross-entropy is −ln q₁, so only the probability on the true class matters: contour lines run parallel to the opposite edge, and how the wrong classes share the rest changes nothing.
loss_shapes.title: Three-class cross-entropy on the probability triangle

loss_shapes.caption: The true class scores 0; the axes are the two rivals' scores. Softmax cross-entropy acts like a smooth maximum: it mostly listens to the strongest rival, so the surface is a rounded corner. With one rival far below, it reduces to the two-score logistic loss.
loss_shapes.title: Softmax cross-entropy over two rival scores

loss_shapes.caption: Weston–Watkins adds up the violation from every rival that comes within the margin of the true class. Where both rivals compete, both count, so the surface rises twice as steeply along the diagonal z₂ = z₃.
loss_shapes.title: Weston–Watkins hinge over two rival scores

loss_shapes.caption: Crammer–Singer counts only the worst rival: the loss is the hinge of the largest rival score. The surface is a fold along z₂ = z₃, where the worst rival switches, and it is half the Weston–Watkins loss where both rivals compete equally.
loss_shapes.title: Crammer–Singer hinge over two rival scores

losses.formula: ½r² if |r| ≤ δ, else δ(|r| − ½δ)

tools.description: Return bevaru's capability manifest, or one section of it (losses, models, datasets, views, loss_shapes, sweep_parameters, experiences, messages, tools, schemas).
tools.name: describe

tools.description: List the registered experiences: id, title, summary, category, kind, and requirements.
tools.name: list_experiences

tools.description: Evaluate losses and their (sub)gradients at points: residuals r = ŷ − y for regression losses, margins m = y·f(x) for classification losses. At most 10000 points.
tools.name: evaluate_losses

tools.description: Sample a 3-D loss-shape view (see the manifest's loss_shapes) on a grid of at most 101 × 101: the axes, every loss value, which values were clipped at the cap, the caption, and the slice that equals the 2-D loss curve.
tools.name: sample_loss_shape

tools.description: Build a dataset and return its displayed coordinates, class labels, axis names, and (for PCA) explained variance. At most 5000 points are returned.
tools.name: build_dataset

tools.description: Train one model on a dataset until it converges or reaches its step budget (at most 100000 steps). Returns the loss trajectory (at most 500 points), final weights and bias, status, and support vectors for SVMs.
tools.name: train

tools.description: Train to convergence at each value of one hyperparameter (2 to 50 values) and return each solution's weights, bias, objective, and support-vector count.
tools.name: sweep

tools.description: Render losses against their argument as a PNG chart.
tools.name: render_loss_chart

tools.description: Render a 3-D loss-shape view as a PNG surface, coloured cool to warm by height, with labelled axes and an optional camera azimuth and elevation.
tools.name: render_loss_shape

tools.description: Train one model and render its training objective by step as a PNG chart.
tools.name: render_training_chart

tools.description: List the experiences registered in the running app.
tools.name: app_list_experiences

tools.description: Start an experience in the running app by id, leaving the current one.
tools.name: app_enter_experience

tools.description: Return the running app to its lobby, cleaning up the current experience.
tools.name: app_leave_experience

tools.description: Send a playback command (play, pause, toggle, step, reset, seek) to every pane of the running experiment.
tools.name: app_playback

tools.description: Start a hyperparameter sweep in the running experiment.

tools.description: Read the running app's state: screen, active experience, panes and their configurations, step, objective, and sweep progress.
